name: Saaspo
tagline: 3,097 SaaS pages filed by page type, section and stack, with 1,115 sites indexed here individually
description: A curated gallery of SaaS web design: 3,097 pages, 716 sections, 379 OG images and 46 templates, filed so you can ask for a specific artefact rather than browse a wall. Pages are filterable by type - landing, pricing, product, about, blog, customers - and by the stack that built them: Webflow, Next.js, Gatsby, Framer, WordPress. Section-level filing is the distinguishing feature: it indexes the parts of a page, so a hero or a pricing table can be found without opening the site it came from. Screenshots are captured with ScreenshotOne. Built by Andy Hooke.
pricing_detail: Free to browse. Carries sponsor slots and affiliate links on sponsored posts.
agent_guidance: Use it when the brief is a SaaS marketing page and you need a peer set rather than a mood. The two filters that matter are page type and stack: asking for pricing pages built in Framer is a different and far more useful question than asking for nice SaaS sites. Section-level filing means a hero or pricing table can be pulled without the whole page. The site itself sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to curl and to headless Chrome alike, so it cannot be scraped - the 1,115 sites indexed here were taken from its listing and screenshotted directly from source.
why_it_matters: Filing by page type and by build stack turns a gallery into a query surface, which is the difference between inspiration and evidence when picking a reference for a specific page.
tier_reason: Large, well-filed and maintained, with section-level granularity and stack filters that almost no other gallery offers. Held below S because it is bot-blocked with no API, so nothing can be verified or refreshed programmatically.
notable_for: filterable by page type and by build stack
section-level filing, not just whole pages
evidence: https://saaspo.com returns 403 Cloudflare to curl and to headless Chrome; counts and filters read from the site listing; 1,115 distinct sites extracted from it
